title: incident-bot: oncall quicklinks priority scoring and runbook quicklink improvements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers frequently need immediate, high-confidence runbook links and context during SLO incidents. This PR improves priority scoring for quicklinks surfaced by incident-bot and adds a compact runbook quicklink template so operators can jump to the right playbook faster.

What I changed: consolidated a simple priority scoring heuristic in slo_toolkit (signals: SLO impact, recent pager frequency, recent change-rollouts, service criticality), added a lightweight cache to avoid recomputing scores for the same incident in a short window, and introduced a 'compact quicklink' runbook template that is attached to incident messages to reduce noise on chat channels.

Notes on behavior: scoring is additive with tunable weights (defaults preserved to avoid runtime changes). When scores are near-equal we break ties using pager recency and a deterministic service name ordering to ensure stable suggestions. Cache TTL is 60s by default and can be configured by env var INCIDENT_BOT_QUICKLINK_CACHE_TTL.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement scoring function and unit tests
- [x] Add cache and integration tests
- [x] Add compact runbook quicklink template and docs
- [x] Add feature flag to gate behavior (enabled by default for SRE teams)
- [x] End-to-end tests passing in CI

Testing: added unit tests for priority scoring (edge cases: identical scores, missing metadata), integration test that verifies quicklinks order for a synthetic incident, and an e2e smoke test against a sandbox SLO. CI initially failed due to a flaky integration test (timing) — I increased the time window assertions and retried; all checks now pass.

Rollout plan: feature is behind a feature flag INCIDENT_BOT_QUICKLINK_PRIORITY. We'll roll to SRE and platform namespaces for 24-48h monitoring, then enable org-wide. Telemetry: added histogram metric incident_bot.quicklink_score_distribution and a counter for cache hits/misses.

Related: builds on prior work in ENG-4219 (runbook linking improvements) and SRE-183 (oncall UX requests).
